subject: FastCart launch load test — 5xx/429 storm & retry amplification

Cc: sre@fastcart.com
Date: 2026-11-01T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: FastCart launch load test — elevated 5xx and timeouts

Hi Marissa / Soojin,

We're in the middle of a planned ramp (stage->prod smoke) and started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and gateway timeouts around 08:00 PST. Traffic was a controlled ramp from 100 qps -> 2k qps over 20 minutes. Within the first 10 minutes we saw intermittent 503/504s and then a sustained 429 wave accompanied by client-side retries that made recovery worse.

I've attached a compressed bundle of sampling logs and our load generator config (fastcart-loadtest-logs.tar.gz). Key observations in our logs:
- 08:03:12 PST: 503 spikes on /v1/generate (spike to ~12% 5xx for ~3m)
- 08:05:20 PST onward: 429s increase to ~9% while latency p50/p95 rose from 120ms/400ms to 350ms/1.8s
- Our client retrier sent exponential backoff but jitter was small, causing many concurrent retries.

We need immediate help to stabilize — we have a go-live window on 2026-11-03 and this is blocking our confidence. Can someone from SRE or platform help triage? We can jump on a call.

Thanks,
Amy Chen
Director of Engineering, FastCart

Subject: Re: FastCart launch load test — elevated 5xx and timeouts

Quick triage notes after looking at the logs and tracing:
- Root cause appears to be retry amplification interacting with the request queue and autoscaler. When burst qps hit the route, task queue depth spiked and we started rejecting with 429; client retries (small jitter) pushed concurrent queued requests back up and some pods hit 5xx timeouts.
- Autoscaler scaled but with a ~45s ramp; during that window CPU and GPU queues saturated and latency spiked.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (low-risk):
1) Apply a temporary route-level ingress rate limit at 1.2x their observed steady qps to stop the retry storm (we can do this by creating a route policy override).
2) Enable request queueing with a 30s soft deadline so we return 429 earlier and avoid long-hanging requests causing 5xx.
3) Route a fraction (10-15%) of traffic to a lower-cost model variant (reduced context length) to reduce per-token compute while we stabilize.
4) Recommend FastCart pause ramp for 1 hour while we apply changes and watch metrics.

I'll prepare the overrides and can apply them with your sign-off, Soojin. Also recommend we capture a short post-mortem and add a recommended client-side backoff jitter to their SDK.

Connor O'Brien
SRE — Serving Runtime

Subject: Executive summary and actions — FastCart load test incident (INC123456)

Team / Execs, forwarding final status and requests ahead of the 11/03 customer sync: 

Summary: During FastCart's controlled ramp on 11/01 we observed retry amplification that produced a sustained 429 wave and transient 5xx/timeouts. We applied temporary mitigations (route rate-limit, queue deadline, 15% route split to reduced-context variant) which stabilized p95 and reduced 5xx to <0.5% within 20 minutes.

What we did:
- Applied ingress rate limit policy (temporary)
- Enabled 30s soft request deadline to limit long-hanging requests
- Routed 15% traffic to model variant 'fc-rt-small' to lower per-token work
- Opened PD incident INC123456 and monitored dashboards (https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/fastcart/overview)

Customer asks:
- Confirmation of eligibility for a one-time credit related to the incident (customer references pilot agreement tied to deal FC-2025-41)
- Timeline for a durable mitigation: Connor proposes a production rollout of autoscaler tuning + improved admission control and client SDK changes (expected 2 weeks for dev/test, 4 weeks for staged rollout).

Next steps:
- Approve customer credit (Marissa please advise on commercial approach).
- Connor to own durable mitigation plan and schedule (deliverable: autoscaler tuning PR + admission control ticket by 2026-11-10).
- 11/03 10:00 PST customer sync (invite sent) — Soojin/Marissa/Connor/Sean to attend.
